questions.q: A user reports "the Incident list is slow." What's the problem with acting on that sentence directly?
options: It contains no measurement — no duration, no frequency, and no indication of who is affected
ServiceNow lists are never actually slow, so the report must be wrong
It means the instance is down entirely
It can only be fixed by contacting ServiceNow Support first
questions.explain: "Slow" without numbers is a feeling, not a diagnosis — there's no way to know which of many possible causes actually matters until you have real data.

questions.q: What does a logged slow-transaction record actually capture?
options: The URL or table involved, the user and session, total duration, and a breakdown of where that time was spent
Only the name of the admin who most recently edited the form
A screenshot of the slow page
The number of fields on the form, regardless of performance
questions.explain: The log is designed to turn a vague complaint into concrete, structured evidence about one specific request.

questions.q: Why is the response-time threshold worth tuning deliberately, rather than leaving at a default forever?
options: A threshold set too low produces a noisy log of mostly ordinary requests; set too high, it misses genuinely slow transactions entirely
The threshold has no real effect on what gets logged
Thresholds are only relevant to database administrators, not ServiceNow admins
Lowering the threshold always deletes older log entries
questions.explain: The threshold is the line between "logged as slow" and "not logged" — too tight and it's noise, too loose and real problems slip through uncaptured.

questions.q: Within a single slow-transaction record, what does the time breakdown let you do?
options: See which portion of the total duration came from scripts, queries, or rendering, rather than just one overall number
Automatically rewrite the slow business rule
Delete the offending transaction from the instance
See the exact line of client-side CSS causing the delay
questions.explain: A transaction's total time is made of several pieces — the breakdown tells you which piece actually dominates, rather than leaving you with a single opaque total.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what should an admin do before changing any UI Policy or Related List configuration in response to a performance complaint?
options: Check the Slow Request Log first, to confirm there's a real, measurable problem and get a rough sense of where the time is going
Immediately disable every UI Policy on the form
Ask the reporting user to clear their browser cache and nothing else
Wait for ServiceNow Support to confirm the issue before looking at anything
questions.explain: The log is the starting point this whole course builds from — confirm and measure the problem before diagnosing a specific cause.
